title: Views of demons in the Dark Medieval
summary: How different folk see the fallen around the 13th century.

claims.text: The Church teaches that demons serve the Devil and steal souls; a few theologians, following Plato, call them go-betweens, and others say their temptations test humanity for God, though such views run against orthodoxy.
Cainites tend to see demons as shadowy rivals who hunt innocent souls and care little for the black souls of vampires.
Mages tend to treat demons as dangerous servants that can be summoned and bound.

title: Thralls must damn themselves
summary: How mortals come to serve demons.

claims.text: Demons may blackmail, deceive, threaten or torture, but they cannot force anyone into service; every thrall finally chooses the bargain.
Like demons, thralls may seek the long road back to grace, but most never try.
Church hunters sort demon servants into three kinds: worshippers, direct servants, and summoners able to bring fiends up out of Hell.

title: Demons posing as gods
summary: Demons that take over established pagan worship.

claims.text: A demon that impersonates a local god inherits a ready-made cult and its rites, needing only a few thralls such as the existing priest.
Rumours of gods walking among the faithful can spread the cult across several neighbouring villages.
Such worship changes slowly, but the willingness of believers to bleed and die gives the demon a steady source of Resolve, and it suits demons bound to a demesne that cannot travel far.

title: Demons as Dark Ages characters
summary: Rules for demons and infernalists in Dark Ages games.

claims.text: Full rules let players and Storytellers create demons and mortal infernalists for Dark Ages games, with new and changed traits for the infernal host.
The rules assume a demon wears a mortal host, with brief notes for Earthbound demons.

title: The Baali as demons see them
summary: The fallen’s view of the Baali bloodline.

claims.text: Cainite lore names the Baali as the first bloodline to break from the thirteen clans, and the clans blame one another for its origin.
The Baali claim to serve the Children, beings older than Christian myth, and scorn any link to Satan; demons find this as childish as Church exaggeration.
As far as demons can tell, the founder came from an abandoned demon cult, perhaps one left over from the age of rebellion, discovered by one of the earliest vampires.
Demons and Baali are often rivals or enemies, each caring more for its own power than for the other.

title: Daimoinon against the fallen
summary: How Baali powers work on demons and thralls.

claims.text: Demons resist with Resolve, and against infernal characters without that protection the difficulty is Resolve + 2; instead of panic, each success inflicts a point of temporary Torment.

Essence of the Netherworld forces a struck demon or thrall to check for degeneration, and Psychomachia makes the victim’s Vice rule the scene, showing demons the monstrous face of their own Apocalyptic Form.
With five successes on severity, Curse tears a demon from a mortal host and bars it from being summoned back for the curse’s duration, though not from an Earthbound reliquary.
Hell-Born Investiture can grant 10 points of approved Arcana per purchase, fuelled by blood instead of Resolve, but never freedom from blood, sunlight or faith.

title: Tear the Rift and summoning
summary: Elder Daimoinon powers for calling demons out of Hell.

claims.text: Tear the Rift costs three blood points and an Intelligence + Occult roll at difficulty 7 with a demon’s Celestial Name, or 5 with its True Name, dragging the demon out in a burst of fire.

A slower technique needs an hour and five points of the user’s vitae for a blood circle, then Intelligence + Occult against the demon’s Resolve + 5, or + 2 with a True Name; above 10 it is impossible and a botch bars that demon for good.
The summoned demon is free of the Abyss’ pull only inside the circle or until sunlight touches the blood, and the technique gives no control; binding needs other magic or mortal acolytes.

Glyphs painted in vitae on a willing or restrained host, reliquary or demesne, with an Intelligence + Occult roll at difficulty 8, lower the difficulty of the demon’s first possession by 1 per success; the technique costs 35 experience.
Its members, mages devoted to demon lore and diabolism, name themselves the Veneficti.
Built on twisting Judeo-Christian ideas such as sin, the order stands opposite the Messianic Voices.
Like the Baali, the Circle bargains with Hell on its own terms and is a rival rather than a servant of the fallen.
